Subject: Proportional rebate & spot-burst structure for Hosted API

Hi Sarah —

Great speaking earlier. As promised, attached is a short proposal (SaaSCo_PRICING_PROPOSAL_v1.pdf) that tries to balance SaaSCo's desire for: lower effective unit price on sustained volume, predictable commit economics for your finance team, and an emergency burst path for unpredictable spikes. High-level: 

- Commit tiers: 200M tokens/month baseline commit (12-month term). Base per-token price: $0.0009.
- Proportional rebate: at renewal we reconcile actual usage vs commit on a quarterly cadence and rebate the delta at a step-down rate (0.5x of incremental pricing) if SaaSCo exceeds committed tiers by >15% consistently.
- Minimum spend floor: 50% of committed monthly value for months 1-3 while you ramp; standard true-up thereafter.
- Overage / on-demand: on-demand will be billed at 1.9x base per-token for over-commit usage.
- Spot / emergency burst: on-demand bursts routed to spare capacity will get a 10% discount off the on-demand overage when capacity available; no SLA for spot.

Notes / asks for you: procurement timeline, whether your legal would accept a quarterly true-up vs annual, and confirm whether we should include a 30k credit as a one-time onboarding concession.

I'll loop in our GTM and pricing folks for specific ladder numbers if you want to discuss next week.

Thanks,

Ben / Karthik — forwarding Sarah's procurement questions. Need quick alignment so I can get back to procurement with a one-page (and a worked example). Key asks: rebate example, spot behavior during sustained spikes, and credit mechanics.

My suggested starting point (cheap attempt):
- Rebate example: If commit = 200M tokens/month at $0.0009, and in Q1 they average 250M (25% over) for 3 months, rebate equals (excess tokens * base price * 0.5). So 50M * $0.0009 * 0.5 = $22.5k applied as credit to renewal.
- If sustained spikes >48h, spot will automatically move to on-demand rate (no discount) after 72 hours continuous usage to protect capacity, but we can set a cap window.
- Onboarding credit: one-time invoice credit applied within first billing cycle; alternatively, can be escrowed against commit if legal prefers.

Attached a quick calc sheet (rebate_calc_sheet.xlsx) with the above. Thoughts?

Jordan

Jordan — good framing. A few practical guardrails from pricing/legal we should use when we reply to procurement: 

- Rebate worked example: your calc is fine; make explicit that rebates are applied at renewal as a credit (not a cash refund) and only if they renew the commit. If they do not renew, rebate converts to a final invoice credit applied to remaining term.
- Minimum spend: recommend a 50% floor of committed monthly value for months 1-3 (startup ramp). After month 3, standard monthly true-up with quarterly reconciliation.
- Overage/on-demand: set on-demand at 1.6x base for this deal (vs 1.9x suggested) to be competitive — but mark it as "during capacity-normal conditions".
- Spot burst: 10% discount off on-demand for bursts <72 consecutive hours. If burst continues >72 hours or sustained utilization impacts capacity, it either moves to on-demand rate or we initiate canary throttling; specify thresholds in SOW.
- Onboarding credit: apply to their first two invoices; if they fall below the 50% floor during ramp, we can offset with the credit so they don't pay upfront true-up immediately.

Putting numbers: commit 200M tokens/month @ $0.0009 = ~$180k ARR commit. On-demand at 1.6x = $0.00144 per token. Spot burst discount = 10% -> $0.001296 per token while spot conditions hold. Rebate example: excess 50M tokens * $0.0009 * 0.5 = $22.5k credit at renewal.

If you want, I can draft the one-page term summary and clean examples.

-Ben
SVP, Sales Ops | Redwood Inference

Thanks for the quick questions. Per internal alignment below, here's a concise one-page summary you can share with procurement (I'll attach a PDF and ship a DocuSign when you confirm):

Summary (proposed)
- Commit: 200M tokens/month, 12-month term. Base price: $0.0009/token.
- Minimum spend floor: 50% of monthly committed value for months 1–3. Quarterly true-ups thereafter.
- On-demand (over-commit) rate: 1.6x base = $0.00144/token (applies when usage exceeds commit in a month).
- Spot / emergency burst: when routed to spare capacity, 10% off the on-demand overage (effective $0.001296/token) for windows <72 consecutive hours. After 72 hours sustained burst, rate moves to on-demand and we may engage throttling/cap enforcement per SOW.
- Proportional rebate: excess usage reconciled quarterly. Rebate amount = excess_tokens * base_price * 0.5. Rebate issued as credit at renewal (or applied to remaining invoices if they don't renew).
- Onboarding concession: $30,000 one-time credit applied across first two invoices.
